Location: plan lines 46–70.

The proposed join would expose an unseen PC’s true position. I reproduced this with the real reducer in the sealed-room scene:

- Before Hide: projection is `unknown / never_observed`; observation history is empty.
- PC successfully Hides at `(7,2)`.
- After Hide: projection remains unknown and history remains empty, but a search memory now contains `lastKnownPosition: (7,2)` and suspicion cells `[(7,2)]`.

The cause is [encounter.ts](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-blind-01/src/combat/encounter.ts:2284): `hiddenNow` bypasses the previously-seen requirement, then memory creation uses the visibility snapshot’s true position. “Reducer-owned” does not establish knowledge provenance.

## D664 — OWNER (2026-09-18 08:27): Question 6 — "Seek cover and dodge unless there is some indication of direction of an enemy"
RULING (verbatim above). Reading, as binding for the BLIND-01 unit: a monster that perceives no enemy (no 'seen'/'located' detection) acts on its KNOWLEDGE: (a) if there is an indication of an enemy's direction — a last-known position in observationHistory, a searchMemory / suspicion region (D420), or another defined knowledge cue the plan enumerates from the single actor-knowledge producer (D625) — it advances/searches toward that indication with the existing move-and-search machinery; (b) if there is NO indication, it SEEKS COVER and DODGES: it moves (positive movement, within its speed) to a reachable cell with the best available cover against the room's open approaches, chosen from the map alone (never from an unseen PC's true position — D476/D545 stand), then takes Dodge; if it already holds the best reachable cover, it Dodges in place. SUPERVISOR CONSEQUENCE, open to the owner's veto: the productivity contract (movement > 0 OR an offensive component with a clear trace) must treat the blind posture — seek-cover-and-Dodge, including Dodge-in-place when already at best cover — as PRODUCTIVE, because it is now the defined useful action for a blind monster; a room is unproductive only if a monster has neither a shot, nor a path to better cover, nor an indication to pursue AND is not already in cover. Sequencing: BLIND-01 is planned now (sol, plan reviewed by astra at HIGH per D627), implemented on a new worktree ../dnd-wt-blind-01 (branch claude/blind-01 from claude/vis-field b94dd732), merged into claude/vis-field and then into claude/cohort-01 before Batch 3 re-runs; COHORT-01 Batch 9's hand derivations (Room-8, composite, speculative) are redone after BLIND-01 because the behaviour they pin changes by design.

8556-## D664 — OWNER (2026-09-18 08:27): Question 6 — "Seek cover and dodge unless there is some indication of direction of an enemy"
8557-RULING (verbatim above). Reading, as binding for the BLIND-01 unit: a monster that perceives no enemy (no 'seen'/'located' detection) acts on its KNOWLEDGE: (a) if there is an indication of an enemy's direction — a last-known position in observationHistory, a searchMemory / suspicion region (D420), or another defined knowledge cue the plan enumerates from the single actor-knowledge producer (D625) — it advances/searches toward that indication with the existing move-and-search machinery; (b) if there is NO indication, it SEEKS COVER and DODGES: it moves (positive movement, within its speed) to a reachable cell with the best available cover against the room's open approaches, chosen from the map alone (never from an unseen PC's true position — D476/D545 stand), then takes Dodge; if it already holds the best reachable cover, it Dodges in place. SUPERVISOR CONSEQUENCE, open to the owner's veto: the productivity contract (movement > 0 OR an offensive component with a clear trace) must treat the blind posture — seek-cover-and-Dodge, including Dodge-in-place when already at best cover — as PRODUCTIVE, because it is now the defined useful action for a blind monster; a room is unproductive only if a monster has neither a shot, nor a path to better cover, nor an indication to pursue AND is not already in cover. Sequencing: BLIND-01 is planned now (sol, plan reviewed by astra at HIGH per D627), implemented on a new worktree ../dnd-wt-blind-01 (branch claude/blind-01 from claude/vis-field b94dd732), merged into claude/vis-field and then into claude/cohort-01 before Batch 3 re-runs; COHORT-01 Batch 9's hand derivations (Room-8, composite, speculative) are redone after BLIND-01 because the behaviour they pin changes by design.

function movementWithBonusUse(
  movement: EngineMovementObjective,
  bonusUse: EngineBonusActionUse,
  speed: number,
): EngineMovementObjective {
  if (bonusUse.kind !== 'dash') return movement;
  return {
    ...movement,
    preference: {
      ...movement.preference,
      willingness: 'freely',
      maximumFeet: (movement.preference.maximumFeet ?? speed) + speed,
    },
  };
}

export interface EngineStandardOfferDeclaration {
  readonly label: string;
  readonly movement: EngineMovementObjective;
  readonly actionSlots: readonly EngineActionSlotUse[];
  readonly resourceCostLabels: readonly string[];
  readonly omittedRiders: readonly EngineOmittedRider[];
  readonly activationChoice: EngineActivationChoiceSlot | null;
}

export function generateStandardOfferDeclarations(
  state: EncounterState,
  actorId: CombatantId,
): readonly EngineStandardOfferDeclaration[] {
  const subject = state.combatants.find((candidate) => candidate.profile.id === actorId);
  if (subject?.profile.kind !== 'monster') return [];
  const bonus = bonusUses(state, actorId);
  return mainUses(state, actorId).flatMap((mainUse) => {
    const mainSlot: EngineActionSlotUse = { slot: 'main', use: mainUse.use };
    return [
      {
        label: mainUse.label,
        movement: mainUse.movement,
        actionSlots: [mainSlot],
        resourceCostLabels: mainUse.resourceCostLabels,
        omittedRiders: mainUse.omittedRiders,
        activationChoice: mainUse.activationChoice ?? null,
      },
      ...bonus.filter((bonusUse) => (mainUse.activationChoice ?? null) === null ||
        (bonusUse.activationChoice ?? null) === null).map((bonusUse): EngineStandardOfferDeclaration => ({
        label: `${mainUse.label} + ${bonusUse.label}`,
        movement: movementWithBonusUse(mainUse.movement, bonusUse.use, subject.profile.rules.speed),
        actionSlots: [mainSlot, { slot: 'bonus', use: bonusUse.use }],
        resourceCostLabels: [...mainUse.resourceCostLabels, ...bonusUse.resourceCostLabels],
        omittedRiders: mainUse.omittedRiders,
        activationChoice: mainUse.activationChoice ?? bonusUse.activationChoice ?? null,
      })),
    ];
  });
}

export const blindActorReferenceSchema = z.strictObject({
  name: blindBoundedNameSchema,
  badge: blindPositiveBadgeSchema,
});
export type BlindActorReference = z.infer<typeof blindActorReferenceSchema>;

export const namedBoardEntitySchema = z.strictObject({
  name: blindBoundedNameSchema,
  badge: blindPositiveBadgeSchema.optional(),
});
export type NamedBoardEntity = z.infer<typeof namedBoardEntitySchema>;

export const blindActionKinds = [
  'attack',
  'cast',
  'interact',
  'dash',
  'dodge',
  'disengage',
  'hide',
  'help',
  'ready',
  'end',
] as const;
export const blindActionKindSchema = z.enum(blindActionKinds);
export type BlindActionKind = z.infer<typeof blindActionKindSchema>;

const namedBlindActionSchema = z.union([
  z.strictObject({ kind: z.literal('attack'), name: blindBoundedNameSchema.optional() }),
  z.strictObject({ kind: z.literal('cast'), name: blindBoundedNameSchema }),
  z.strictObject({ kind: z.literal('interact'), name: blindBoundedNameSchema.optional() }),
): BoundEntity | 'unknown' | 'ambiguous' {
  const matches = entityCandidates(state, projection, reference, kind);
  if (matches.length === 0) return 'unknown';
  if (matches.length > 1) return 'ambiguous';
  return matches[0] ?? 'unknown';
}

function actionDisplayName(
  state: EncounterState,
  actorId: CombatantId,
  slot: EngineActionSlotUse,
  queries: EngineQueryPort,
): string | null {
  const use = slot.use;
  switch (use.kind) {
    case 'attack':
    case 'multiattack':
    case 'saving_throw': {
      const sources = slot.slot === 'main'
        ? queries.actions(state, actorId)
        : monsterBonusActions(state, actorId);
      const source = sources.find((action) => 'id' in action && action.id === use.actionId);
      if (source === undefined) return String(use.actionId);
      if ('name' in source && typeof source.name === 'string') return source.name;
      return source.kind === 'multiattack' ? 'Multiattack' : String(use.actionId);
    }
    case 'cast_spell': return spellDefinition(use.spellId)?.name ?? String(use.spellId);
    case 'use_world_object': return String(use.actionId);
    case 'dodge': return 'Dodge';
    case 'disengage': return 'Disengage';
    case 'dash': return 'Dash';
    case 'hide': return 'Hide';
    case 'end_turn': return 'End Turn';
  }
}

function actionKind(slot: EngineActionSlotUse): BlindActionKind {
  switch (slot.use.kind) {
    case 'attack':
    case 'multiattack':
    case 'saving_throw': return 'attack';
    case 'cast_spell': return 'cast';
    case 'use_world_object': return 'interact';
    case 'dodge': return 'dodge';
    case 'disengage': return 'disengage';
    case 'dash': return 'dash';
    case 'hide': return 'hide';
    case 'end_turn': return 'end';
  }
}

Date: 2026-09-18

D420, D476, D545, D617, D625, D632, D636.6, D641-D643, and D662-D664.

## 1. Outcome, sequencing, and invariants
Implement D664 exactly: when a monster perceives an enemy, retain normal offers; when it perceives
none but has an actor-known directional indication, move and Search toward that indication; when it
has no indication, move at normal speed to the best topology-only cover available against the room's
open approaches and take Dodge. If its current cell is already tied for best reachable cover, take
Dodge without moving. Both forms of the blind posture are productive.

Hard invariants:
- Never read an unperceived PC token, current position, distance, or route. D476/D545 remain intact.
- `projectActorKnowledge` remains the single actor-knowledge producer (D625). Offer code must not
  inspect `observationHistory` or `searchMemories` independently.
- The resolver calls only its injected `environment.queries`; it must not import or construct the
  canonical query port, movement world, terrain helpers, or cover tracer (D617.5).
- No fixture byte changes. No expectation may be copied from changed-code output. Unchanged fields
  may be carried from the pre-change `b94dd732` tree; every changed behavioral value is hand-derived.
- `generateRoom` does not consult offers: `src/vtt/room-generator.ts:1426` and
  `tools/generate-arena-basis.ts:251-345` have no offer/resolver/query-port import. All 42 currently
  tracked generated rooms must remain byte-identical; BLIND-01 does not regenerate them.
- No full Vitest, Playwright, build, browser server, or port 4173. Use only the targeted commands below.

Sequencing/ownership:
1. Implement B1-B4 on the stated base. Merge the accepted core into `claude/vis-field`, then into
   `claude/cohort-01` before COHORT-01 Batch 3 re-runs, as D664 requires.
2. COHORT-01 then creates/lands its already-authorized v2/v6 code surface; apply B5-B6 against that
   rebased tip. This is not permission to alter v1/v5 rows or any fixture bytes.
3. `src/vtt/intent-resolver.ts`, `src/vtt/turn-proposal.ts`, and
   `src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts` are also owned by ELEVATION-02's 221-path manifest (D636.6) and the
   D584 72-path inventory. The supervisor must record: `BLIND-01 landed first; ELEVATION_BASE_REV
   includes BLIND-01; ELEVATION-02 must rebase, retain pursue_indication/seek_cover/search and the
   cover query, and rerun both ownership overlays before B0.` A conflict may not silently drop them.

## 2. Knowledge branching
Current facts are at `src/vtt/intel/actor-knowledge.ts:42-90,98-123,226-289` and
`src/combat/search-memory.ts:15-64,88-101,103-150`.

Add a typed, internal `projectActorTurnKnowledge(state, actorId)` beside
`projectActorKnowledge`. It first consumes that projection, then joins only active reducer-owned
`SearchMemory` rows for the actor. It returns one closed union:

| Knowledge outcome | Directional indication | Offer branch |
|---|---|---|
| At least one `perceived` target (`seen` or mechanically `located`) | Current actor-known position | `normal`; call the existing normal declaration path unchanged. Do not also emit blind/pursuit offers. |
| No perceived target; active `SearchMemory` for a living opponent | Existing `lastKnownPosition`, `suspicion.cells`, and the existing `legalOptions` | `pursue_indication`; one option per memory containing `move_and_search`. |
| No perceived target; `suspected` target with observation-history `lastSeenPosition`, but no memory for that pair | That historical singleton cell | `pursue_indication`; one option for the observation. |
| `unknown` / `never_observed` | None | Contributes no cue. |
| `placement_pending` | None | Contributes no cue; pending placement never exposes a position. |
| No perceived targets and no cues after the preceding rows | None | `blind_posture` (`seek_cover` + Dodge). |

Those are all cues defined today. There is no hearing marker, alert vector, nearest-enemy fallback,
party centroid, initiative inference, or unseen-token cue; do not invent one. For the same target, an
active memory supersedes its duplicate observation-history cue because it owns the expanding region.
Memories exist only for hiding, invisibility, or obscurement; `blocked` and `out_of_range` create none.
Sort independent cues by target id, source (`search_memory` before `observation_history`), then
row/column; emit each rather than guessing which enemy matters.

Reuse rather than duplicate D420 machinery:

- For a memory, select its existing `legalOptions` member with `kind: 'move_and_search'`; carry that
  typed member and its existing Search citation into the pursuit objective. Use the existing
  `suspicion.cells` verbatim. Never recreate the region, radius, roll mode, or citations in offers.
- The pursue destination minimizes distance to any indicated cell, then path cost, row, column,
  using query-port results. It moves no farther than normal speed and then issues the existing
  `{type:'search', actor, target, reliance:'sight'}` command (`src/combat/events.ts:95-100` and
  `src/combat/encounter.ts:4820-4857`). Reaching the indication is not required in one turn.
- Existing `attack_suspected_square` entries, their exact `cells`, forced Disadvantage, and reducer
  command (`src/combat/events.ts:216-228`, `src/combat/encounter.ts:7457`) remain the sole machinery
  for that escalation. BLIND-01 does not clone them into a second shape; Q2 below decides whether
  standard offers should expose them at all.

## 3. Topology-only cover objective

### 3.1 Open approaches

Compute the same stable row-major set for every candidate, entirely inside the canonical query-port
implementation, from `bounds`, `blockedCells`, and `worldObjects`:

1. **Unblocked frontier:** every in-bounds boundary cell whose effective terrain passability is not
   `blocked`.
2. **Open doorway:** every in-bounds/passable footprint cell of a world object with `kind:'door'` and
   `blocking.movement === false`.
3. **Wall-structure aperture:** every in-bounds/passable cell whose immediate north+south neighbors
   are both in `terrainWallCells(state)`, or whose immediate west+east neighbors are both wall cells.
   This is the exact one-cell aperture in an otherwise continuous cardinal wall; an out-of-bounds
   neighbor does not count. Wider boundary openings are already frontier; authored doors are row 2.

Deduplicate by `column,row` and sort row then column. Closed doors and blocked cells are not
approaches. If the set is empty, every destination has the same empty profile and the origin wins.

### 3.2 Candidates, score, and tie order

Add one `EngineQueryPort` method, `seekCover(state, request)`, to
`src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts:203-251`; the resolver only invokes
`environment.queries.seekCover`. Its result contains the selected legal path/cost/destination plus
approaches and score evidence for tests. Inside the canonical port:

- Candidate anchors are the origin plus every in-bounds anchor for which the actor's full footprint
  fits and the existing canonical `path` query returns legal under `movement:'normal'` and
  `maximumFeet <= current speed`. The returned path and cost are used; no second movement world or
  geometric reach approximation is allowed (`engine-query-port.ts:1060-1131`).
- For each `(destination, approach)`, call existing `traceTerrainLine` (`src/combat/cover.ts:795-802`).
  It includes `blockedCells`, world objects, the physical tier kernel also exposed by
  `coverTierBetweenObjects` (`cover.ts:870-913`), and D635/D642/D657 optical solid-wall rules.
- Encode one approach strength as `[blocksSight ? 1 : 0, coverRank(tier)]`, with ranks
  none=0, half=1, three-quarters=2, total=3. Sort a destination's strengths weakest-first. Compare
  equal-length vectors lexicographically, largest value winning: maximize the worst protected open
  approach, then the next-worst, and so on. This makes an optically sealed line stronger than a
  visible line at the same/lower physical tier; Q1 is the only alternative.
- Select the maximum profile. If origin has that profile, select origin (movement 0). Otherwise use
  lowest actual path cost, then lower row, then lower column. Thus a merely equal cell never causes
  motion, while a strictly better cell does.

### 3.3 Hand oracle used before implementation

Use a 9x5 scene: outer perimeter blocked except `(0,2)`; a full-height wall at column 6 seals a PC
at `(7,2)` from the monster; a passable half-cover object occupies `(2,2)`; monster starts `(1,2)`,
speed 30; no history/memory. The only open approach is `(0,2)`.

| Destination group | Canonical path cost | Trace from `(0,2)` | Profile |
|---|---:|---|---|
| origin `(1,2)` and `(2,2)` | 0 / 10 (enter difficult half cover) | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
| `(3,2)` | 10 via an open diagonal around `(2,2)` | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
| `(4,2)`, `(5,2)` | 15, 20 | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
| reachable `(1..5,1)` and `(1..5,3)` | 5-20 | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |

Therefore choose `(3,2)`, then Dodge. The query-port test must first verify every table trace directly
against `traceTerrainLine` and the half-cover object against `coverTierBetweenObjects`; it may not
obtain this expectation from `seekCover`. With the monster starting at `(3,2)`, origin ties the other
half-cover cells and must win at cost 0, followed by Dodge. This is the sealed-wall RED pair.

action unions. The offer/executor flow is:

typed pursuit. `basic_advance` (`src/vtt/snippets/registry.ts:158-202`) recognizes
`pursue_indication` and `seek_cover` as advance options before its defense fallback; ordinary offense
still wins. The existing Dash declaration (`offer-declarations.ts:497-506`) remains only in the normal

`engineOfferableOption` hashes the canonical offer body (`src/vtt/option-modeling.ts:26-33`), so new

## 5. Productivity contract

Replace the duplicated predicate with one exported structural helper owned by
`tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:272-283`; the active v2 suite at
`tests/unit/vtt/arena-basis-brutal-v2.test.ts:77-104` and the brutal-b membership test call it.
A valid option is productive iff at least one holds:

1. existing positive movement, attack, saving throw, cast, or world-object action;
2. main Search paired with `pursue_indication` (movement may be 0 if already in the region); or
3. exactly one main Dodge paired with `seek_cover`, whether movement is positive or 0.

An arbitrary stationary Dodge remains unproductive. A room is unproductive precisely when at least
one living monster has no valid option in any of those three classes. Consequently a no-indication
monster already at best cover is productive; inability to improve cover is not failure. An unplaced,
action-spent, or otherwise invalid actor remains unproductive if no posture resolves.

-## 3. Topology-only cover objective
-
-### 3.1 Open approaches
-
-Compute the same stable row-major set for every candidate, entirely inside the canonical query-port
-implementation, from `bounds`, `blockedCells`, and `worldObjects`:
-
-1. **Unblocked frontier:** every in-bounds boundary cell whose effective terrain passability is not
-   `blocked`.
-2. **Open doorway:** every in-bounds/passable footprint cell of a world object with `kind:'door'` and
-   `blocking.movement === false`.
-3. **Wall-structure aperture:** every in-bounds/passable cell whose immediate north+south neighbors
-   are both in `terrainWallCells(state)`, or whose immediate west+east neighbors are both wall cells.
-   This is the exact one-cell aperture in an otherwise continuous cardinal wall; an out-of-bounds
-   neighbor does not count. Wider boundary openings are already frontier; authored doors are row 2.
-
-Deduplicate by `column,row` and sort row then column. Closed doors and blocked cells are not
-approaches. If the set is empty, every destination has the same empty profile and the origin wins.
-

-`src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts:203-251`; the resolver only invokes
-`environment.queries.seekCover`. Its result contains the selected legal path/cost/destination plus
-approaches and score evidence for tests. Inside the canonical port:
-
-- Candidate anchors are the origin plus every in-bounds anchor for which the actor's full footprint
-  fits and the existing canonical `path` query returns legal under `movement:'normal'` and
-  `maximumFeet <= current speed`. The returned path and cost are used; no second movement world or
-  geometric reach approximation is allowed (`engine-query-port.ts:1060-1131`).
-- For each `(destination, approach)`, call existing `traceTerrainLine` (`src/combat/cover.ts:795-802`).
-  It includes `blockedCells`, world objects, the physical tier kernel also exposed by
-  `coverTierBetweenObjects` (`cover.ts:870-913`), and D635/D642/D657 optical solid-wall rules.
-- Encode one approach strength as `[blocksSight ? 1 : 0, coverRank(tier)]`, with ranks
-  none=0, half=1, three-quarters=2, total=3. Sort a destination's strengths weakest-first. Compare
-  equal-length vectors lexicographically, largest value winning: maximize the worst protected open
-  approach, then the next-worst, and so on. This makes an optically sealed line stronger than a
-  visible line at the same/lower physical tier; Q1 is the only alternative.
-- Select the maximum profile. If origin has that profile, select origin (movement 0). Otherwise use
-  lowest actual path cost, then lower row, then lower column. Thus a merely equal cell never causes
-  motion, while a strictly better cell does.

-## 3. Topology-only cover objective
-
-### 3.1 Open approaches
-
-Compute the same stable row-major set for every candidate, entirely inside the canonical query-port
-implementation, from `bounds`, `blockedCells`, and `worldObjects`:
-
-1. **Unblocked frontier:** every in-bounds boundary cell whose effective terrain passability is not
-   `blocked`.
-2. **Open doorway:** every in-bounds/passable footprint cell of a world object with `kind:'door'` and
-   `blocking.movement === false`.
-3. **Wall-structure aperture:** every in-bounds/passable cell whose immediate north+south neighbors
-   are both in `terrainWallCells(state)`, or whose immediate west+east neighbors are both wall cells.
-   This is the exact one-cell aperture in an otherwise continuous cardinal wall; an out-of-bounds
-   neighbor does not count. Wider boundary openings are already frontier; authored doors are row 2.
-
-Deduplicate by `column,row` and sort row then column. Closed doors and blocked cells are not
-approaches. If the set is empty, every destination has the same empty profile and the origin wins.
-
-### 3.2 Candidates, score, and tie order
-
-Add one `EngineQueryPort` method, `seekCover(state, request)`, to
-`src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts:203-251`; the resolver only invokes
-`environment.queries.seekCover`. Its result contains the selected legal path/cost/destination plus
-approaches and score evidence for tests. Inside the canonical port:
-
-- Candidate anchors are the origin plus every in-bounds anchor for which the actor's full footprint
-  fits and the existing canonical `path` query returns legal under `movement:'normal'` and
-  `maximumFeet <= current speed`. The returned path and cost are used; no second movement world or
-  geometric reach approximation is allowed (`engine-query-port.ts:1060-1131`).
-- For each `(destination, approach)`, call existing `traceTerrainLine` (`src/combat/cover.ts:795-802`).
-  It includes `blockedCells`, world objects, the physical tier kernel also exposed by
-  `coverTierBetweenObjects` (`cover.ts:870-913`), and D635/D642/D657 optical solid-wall rules.
-- Encode one approach strength as `[blocksSight ? 1 : 0, coverRank(tier)]`, with ranks
-  none=0, half=1, three-quarters=2, total=3. Sort a destination's strengths weakest-first. Compare
-  equal-length vectors lexicographically, largest value winning: maximize the worst protected open
-  approach, then the next-worst, and so on. This makes an optically sealed line stronger than a
-  visible line at the same/lower physical tier; Q1 is the only alternative.
-- Select the maximum profile. If origin has that profile, select origin (movement 0). Otherwise use
-  lowest actual path cost, then lower row, then lower column. Thus a merely equal cell never causes
-  motion, while a strictly better cell does.
-
-### 3.3 Hand oracle used before implementation
-
-Use a 9x5 scene: outer perimeter blocked except `(0,2)`; a full-height wall at column 6 seals a PC
-at `(7,2)` from the monster; a passable half-cover object occupies `(2,2)`; monster starts `(1,2)`,
-speed 30; no history/memory. The only open approach is `(0,2)`.
-
-| Destination group | Canonical path cost | Trace from `(0,2)` | Profile |
-|---|---:|---|---|
-| origin `(1,2)` and `(2,2)` | 0 / 10 (enter difficult half cover) | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
-| `(3,2)` | 10 via an open diagonal around `(2,2)` | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
-| `(4,2)`, `(5,2)` | 15, 20 | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
-| reachable `(1..5,1)` and `(1..5,3)` | 5-20 | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
-
-Therefore choose `(3,2)`, then Dodge. The query-port test must first verify every table trace directly
-against `traceTerrainLine` and the half-cover object against `coverTierBetweenObjects`; it may not
-obtain this expectation from `seekCover`. With the monster starting at `(3,2)`, origin ties the other
-half-cover cells and must win at cost 0, followed by Dodge. This is the sealed-wall RED pair.

-## 5. Productivity contract
-
-Replace the duplicated predicate with one exported structural helper owned by
-`tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:272-283`; the active v2 suite at
-`tests/unit/vtt/arena-basis-brutal-v2.test.ts:77-104` and the brutal-b membership test call it.
-A valid option is productive iff at least one holds:
-
-1. existing positive movement, attack, saving throw, cast, or world-object action;
-2. main Search paired with `pursue_indication` (movement may be 0 if already in the region); or
-3. exactly one main Dodge paired with `seek_cover`, whether movement is positive or 0.
-
-An arbitrary stationary Dodge remains unproductive. A room is unproductive precisely when at least
-one living monster has no valid option in any of those three classes. Consequently a no-indication
-monster already at best cover is productive; inability to improve cover is not failure. An unplaced,
-action-spent, or otherwise invalid actor remains unproductive if no posture resolves.

   157	function armorClassKnowledge(

   173	  return target.wildShape?.physical.hitPoints ?? target.form?.hitPoints ?? target.hitPoints;
   174	}

   176	function activeHitPointMaximum(
   177	  state: EncounterState,
   178	  target: EncounterCombatantState,
   179	): number {
   180	  const base = target.wildShape?.physical.hitPointMaximum ??
   181	    target.form?.hitPointMaximum ??
   182	    target.profile.rules.hitPointMaximum;
   183	  return state.effects.reduce((maximum, effect) =>
   184	    effect.targets.includes(target.profile.id) && effect.payload.kind === 'hit_point_maximum_modifier'
   185	      ? maximum + effect.payload.amount
   186	      : maximum, base);
   187	}

   189	// ART-SEAM (D516): exported so the DM board's HP bar uses THIS classifier, never a re-derived threshold.
   190	export function hitPointKnowledge(
   191	  state: EncounterState,
   192	  target: EncounterCombatantState,
   193	): ProjectedHitPointKnowledge {
   194	  const maximum = activeHitPointMaximum(state, target);
   195	  if (maximum <= 0) return { kind: 'unknown' };
   196	  const hitPoints = activeHitPoints(target);
   197	  return {
   198	    kind: 'perceived_band',
   199	    band: hitPoints >= maximum
   200	      ? 'uninjured'
   201	      : hitPoints * 4 <= maximum
   202	        ? 'near_death'
   203	        : 'bloodied',
   204	  };
   205	}

   207	function reactionKnowledge(
   208	  state: EncounterState,
   209	  targetId: CombatantId,
   210	): ProjectedReactionKnowledge {
   211	  const latestTurnStart = state.eventLog.reduce((latest, event) =>
   212	    event.type === 'turn_started' && event.combatant === targetId
   213	      ? Math.max(latest, event.sequence)
   214	      : latest, -1);
   215	  return state.eventLog.some((event) =>
   216	    event.sequence > latestTurnStart && event.type === 'resource_spent' &&
   217	    event.combatant === targetId && event.resource === 'reaction')
   218	    ? { kind: 'observed_spent' }
   219	    : { kind: 'unknown' };
   220	}

   222	/**
   223	 * Projects living opponents as one actor can currently locate them, falling
   224	 * back only to reducer-owned observation history.
   225	 */
   226	export function projectActorKnowledge(
   227	  state: EncounterState,
   228	  actorId: CombatantId,
   229	): ActorKnowledgeProjection {
   230	  if (!state.combatants.some((combatant) => combatant.profile.id === actorId)) {
   231	    throw new RangeError(`Actor knowledge requires a combatant in this encounter: ${String(actorId)}.`);
   232	  }
   233	  const tokens = new Map(state.tokens.map((token) => [token.combatantId, token] as const));
   234	  const actorIsPlaced = tokens.has(actorId) && !state.adjudicationPending.some((entry) =>
   235	    entry.combatant === actorId);
   236	  const targets = state.combatants
   237	    .filter((candidate) => candidate.life !== 'dead' &&
   238	      !combatantsAreAllies(state, actorId, candidate.profile.id))
   239	    .map((candidate): ActorTargetKnowledge => {
   240	      const targetId = candidate.profile.id;
   241	      const target = tokens.get(targetId);
   242	      const pending = state.adjudicationPending.find((entry) =>
   243	        entry.combatant === targetId);
   244	      if (pending !== undefined) {
   245	        return {
   246	          kind: 'placement_pending',
   247	          placementStatus: 'placement_pending',
   248	          targetId,
   249	          pendingReason: pending.kind,
   250	        };
   251	      }
   252	      if (target === undefined) {
   253	        return unlocatedTarget(state, actorId, targetId);
   254	      }
   255	      if (!actorIsPlaced) return unlocatedTarget(state, actorId, targetId);
   256	
   257	      const space = combatantSpace(state, targetId);
   258	      const detection = detectCombatant(state, actorId, targetId);
   259	      if (detection.kind === 'seen' || detection.kind === 'located') {
   260	        const reciprocal = detectCombatant(state, targetId, actorId);
   261	        const seen = detection.kind === 'seen';
   262	        return {
   263	          kind: 'perceived',
   264	          placementStatus: 'placed',
   265	          targetId,
   266	          position: { ...target.position },
   267	          effectiveSize: effectiveCreatureSize(state, targetId),
   268	          placementMode: structuredClone(target.placementMode),
   269	          footprint: space.cells.map((cell) => ({ ...cell })) as [GridCell, ...GridCell[]],
   270	          distanceFeet: minimumSpaceDistance(combatantSpace(state, actorId), space),
   271	          conditions: seen ? perceivedConditions(state, targetId) : [],
   272	          armorClass: seen ? armorClassKnowledge(state, targetId) : { kind: 'unknown' },
   273	          hitPoints: seen ? hitPointKnowledge(state, candidate) : { kind: 'unknown' },
   274	          reciprocalVisibility: reciprocal.kind === 'seen'
   275	            ? { kind: 'perceived', targetCanSeeActor: true }
   276	            : { kind: 'unknown' },
   277	          reaction: reactionKnowledge(state, targetId),
   278	        };
   279	      }
   280	      return unlocatedTarget(state, actorId, targetId);
   281	    })
   282	    .sort((left, right) => String(left.targetId).localeCompare(String(right.targetId)));
   283	
   284	  return {
   285	    policy: ACTOR_KNOWLEDGE_POLICY,
   286	    actorId,
   287	    targets,
   288	  };
   289	}

   294	}

    71	/** A clipped Chebyshev radius matches the engine's eight-way 5-foot grid distance. */
    72	export function suspicionCells(
    73	  bounds: GridBounds,
    74	  center: GridCell,
    75	  radius: Feet,
    76	): readonly GridCell[] {
    77	  if (!isCellInside(bounds, center)) throw new RangeError('A suspicion-region center must be on the grid.');
    78	  const cells: GridCell[] = [];
    79	  for (let row = 0; row < bounds.rows; row += 1) {
    80	    for (let column = 0; column < bounds.columns; column += 1) {
    81	      const candidate = { column, row };
    82	      if (gridDistance(center, candidate) <= radius) cells.push(candidate);
    83	    }
    84	  }
    85	  return orderedCells(cells);
    86	}

   147	      cells,

-# BLIND-01 implementation plan
-
-Date: 2026-09-18  
-Planning base: `/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-blind-01`, branch
-`claude/blind-01`, commit `b94dd73221697e3d03da8991746726563777fa74`.  
-Authoritative decisions: `/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-multiclass-spells-static/.claude/decisions.md`
-D420, D476, D545, D617, D625, D632, D636.6, D641-D643, and D662-D664.
-All paths below are relative to `/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-blind-01` unless an
-absolute path is printed.
-
-## 1. Outcome, sequencing, and invariants
-Implement D664 exactly: when a monster perceives an enemy, retain normal offers; when it perceives
-none but has an actor-known directional indication, move and Search toward that indication; when it
-has no indication, move at normal speed to the best topology-only cover available against the room's
-open approaches and take Dodge. If its current cell is already tied for best reachable cover, take
-Dodge without moving. Both forms of the blind posture are productive.
-
-Hard invariants:
-- Never read an unperceived PC token, current position, distance, or route. D476/D545 remain intact.
-- `projectActorKnowledge` remains the single actor-knowledge producer (D625). Offer code must not
-  inspect `observationHistory` or `searchMemories` independently.
-- The resolver calls only its injected `environment.queries`; it must not import or construct the
-  canonical query port, movement world, terrain helpers, or cover tracer (D617.5).
-- No fixture byte changes. No expectation may be copied from changed-code output. Unchanged fields
-  may be carried from the pre-change `b94dd732` tree; every changed behavioral value is hand-derived.
-- `generateRoom` does not consult offers: `src/vtt/room-generator.ts:1426` and
-  `tools/generate-arena-basis.ts:251-345` have no offer/resolver/query-port import. All 42 currently
-  tracked generated rooms must remain byte-identical; BLIND-01 does not regenerate them.
-- No full Vitest, Playwright, build, browser server, or port 4173. Use only the targeted commands below.
-
-Sequencing/ownership:
-1. Implement B1-B4 on the stated base. Merge the accepted core into `claude/vis-field`, then into
-   `claude/cohort-01` before COHORT-01 Batch 3 re-runs, as D664 requires.
-2. COHORT-01 then creates/lands its already-authorized v2/v6 code surface; apply B5-B6 against that
-   rebased tip. This is not permission to alter v1/v5 rows or any fixture bytes.
-3. `src/vtt/intent-resolver.ts`, `src/vtt/turn-proposal.ts`, and
-   `src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts` are also owned by ELEVATION-02's 221-path manifest (D636.6) and the
-   D584 72-path inventory. The supervisor must record: `BLIND-01 landed first; ELEVATION_BASE_REV
-   includes BLIND-01; ELEVATION-02 must rebase, retain pursue_indication/seek_cover/search and the
-   cover query, and rerun both ownership overlays before B0.` A conflict may not silently drop them.
-
-## 2. Knowledge branching
-Current facts are at `src/vtt/intel/actor-knowledge.ts:42-90,98-123,226-289` and
-`src/combat/search-memory.ts:15-64,88-101,103-150`.
-
-Add a typed, internal `projectActorTurnKnowledge(state, actorId)` beside
-`projectActorKnowledge`. It first consumes that projection, then joins only active reducer-owned
-`SearchMemory` rows for the actor. It returns one closed union:
-
-| Knowledge outcome | Directional indication | Offer branch |
-|---|---|---|
-| At least one `perceived` target (`seen` or mechanically `located`) | Current actor-known position | `normal`; call the existing normal declaration path unchanged. Do not also emit blind/pursuit offers. |
-| No perceived target; active `SearchMemory` for a living opponent | Existing `lastKnownPosition`, `suspicion.cells`, and the existing `legalOptions` | `pursue_indication`; one option per memory containing `move_and_search`. |
-| No perceived target; `suspected` target with observation-history `lastSeenPosition`, but no memory for that pair | That historical singleton cell | `pursue_indication`; one option for the observation. |
-| `unknown` / `never_observed` | None | Contributes no cue. |
-| `placement_pending` | None | Contributes no cue; pending placement never exposes a position. |
-| No perceived targets and no cues after the preceding rows | None | `blind_posture` (`seek_cover` + Dodge). |
-
-Those are all cues defined today. There is no hearing marker, alert vector, nearest-enemy fallback,
-party centroid, initiative inference, or unseen-token cue; do not invent one. For the same target, an
-active memory supersedes its duplicate observation-history cue because it owns the expanding region.
-Memories exist only for hiding, invisibility, or obscurement; `blocked` and `out_of_range` create none.
-Sort independent cues by target id, source (`search_memory` before `observation_history`), then
-row/column; emit each rather than guessing which enemy matters.
-
-Reuse rather than duplicate D420 machinery:
-
-- For a memory, select its existing `legalOptions` member with `kind: 'move_and_search'`; carry that
-  typed member and its existing Search citation into the pursuit objective. Use the existing
-  `suspicion.cells` verbatim. Never recreate the region, radius, roll mode, or citations in offers.
-- The pursue destination minimizes distance to any indicated cell, then path cost, row, column,
-  using query-port results. It moves no farther than normal speed and then issues the existing
-  `{type:'search', actor, target, reliance:'sight'}` command (`src/combat/events.ts:95-100` and
-  `src/combat/encounter.ts:4820-4857`). Reaching the indication is not required in one turn.
-- Existing `attack_suspected_square` entries, their exact `cells`, forced Disadvantage, and reducer
-  command (`src/combat/events.ts:216-228`, `src/combat/encounter.ts:7457`) remain the sole machinery
-  for that escalation. BLIND-01 does not clone them into a second shape; Q2 below decides whether
-  standard offers should expose them at all.
-
-## 3. Topology-only cover objective
-
-### 3.1 Open approaches
-
-Compute the same stable row-major set for every candidate, entirely inside the canonical query-port
-implementation, from `bounds`, `blockedCells`, and `worldObjects`:
-
-1. **Unblocked frontier:** every in-bounds boundary cell whose effective terrain passability is not
-   `blocked`.
-2. **Open doorway:** every in-bounds/passable footprint cell of a world object with `kind:'door'` and
-   `blocking.movement === false`.
-3. **Wall-structure aperture:** every in-bounds/passable cell whose immediate north+south neighbors
-   are both in `terrainWallCells(state)`, or whose immediate west+east neighbors are both wall cells.
-   This is the exact one-cell aperture in an otherwise continuous cardinal wall; an out-of-bounds
-   neighbor does not count. Wider boundary openings are already frontier; authored doors are row 2.
-
-Deduplicate by `column,row` and sort row then column. Closed doors and blocked cells are not
-approaches. If the set is empty, every destination has the same empty profile and the origin wins.
-
-### 3.2 Candidates, score, and tie order
-
-Add one `EngineQueryPort` method, `seekCover(state, request)`, to
-`src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts:203-251`; the resolver only invokes
-`environment.queries.seekCover`. Its result contains the selected legal path/cost/destination plus
-approaches and score evidence for tests. Inside the canonical port:
-
-- Candidate anchors are the origin plus every in-bounds anchor for which the actor's full footprint
-  fits and the existing canonical `path` query returns legal under `movement:'normal'` and
-  `maximumFeet <= current speed`. The returned path and cost are used; no second movement world or
-  geometric reach approximation is allowed (`engine-query-port.ts:1060-1131`).
-- For each `(destination, approach)`, call existing `traceTerrainLine` (`src/combat/cover.ts:795-802`).
-  It includes `blockedCells`, world objects, the physical tier kernel also exposed by
-  `coverTierBetweenObjects` (`cover.ts:870-913`), and D635/D642/D657 optical solid-wall rules.
-- Encode one approach strength as `[blocksSight ? 1 : 0, coverRank(tier)]`, with ranks
-  none=0, half=1, three-quarters=2, total=3. Sort a destination's strengths weakest-first. Compare
-  equal-length vectors lexicographically, largest value winning: maximize the worst protected open
-  approach, then the next-worst, and so on. This makes an optically sealed line stronger than a
-  visible line at the same/lower physical tier; Q1 is the only alternative.
-- Select the maximum profile. If origin has that profile, select origin (movement 0). Otherwise use
-  lowest actual path cost, then lower row, then lower column. Thus a merely equal cell never causes
-  motion, while a strictly better cell does.
-
-### 3.3 Hand oracle used before implementation
-
-Use a 9x5 scene: outer perimeter blocked except `(0,2)`; a full-height wall at column 6 seals a PC
-at `(7,2)` from the monster; a passable half-cover object occupies `(2,2)`; monster starts `(1,2)`,
-speed 30; no history/memory. The only open approach is `(0,2)`.
-
-| Destination group | Canonical path cost | Trace from `(0,2)` | Profile |
-|---|---:|---|---|
-| origin `(1,2)` and `(2,2)` | 0 / 10 (enter difficult half cover) | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
-| `(3,2)` | 10 via an open diagonal around `(2,2)` | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
-| `(4,2)`, `(5,2)` | 15, 20 | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
-| reachable `(1..5,1)` and `(1..5,3)` | 5-20 | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
-
-Therefore choose `(3,2)`, then Dodge. The query-port test must first verify every table trace directly
-against `traceTerrainLine` and the half-cover object against `coverTierBetweenObjects`; it may not
-obtain this expectation from `seekCover`. With the monster starting at `(3,2)`, origin ties the other
-half-cover cells and must win at cost 0, followed by Dodge. This is the sealed-wall RED pair.
-
-## 4. Offer and execution shape
-
-Make `EngineEngagement` at `src/vtt/turn-proposal.ts:109-123` a discriminated union with:
-
-- existing target stances unchanged;
-- `{stance:'pursue_indication', indication: KnownIndication}` where the typed indication contains
-  only observation/search-memory knowledge and never a current unseen position; and
-- `{stance:'seek_cover', objective:{kind:'open_approach_cover', policy:'blind-cover-v1'}}`, with no
-  anchor, target, cell, or selector.
-
-Add main action `{kind:'search', targetId, reliance:'sight'}` and resolved `search` to the closed
-action unions. The offer/executor flow is:
-
-- Pursuit: normal-speed movement objective + main Search. Resolve the indicated region through
-  injected queries, move, then execute the existing Search reducer command.
-- Blind posture: normal-speed `seek_cover` objective + main Dodge, label `Seek Cover + Dodge`.
-  `engine-round-session.ts:248-315` already applies movement before action. This is not Dash+Dodge:
-  Dash and Dodge both consume the one main slot; Dash is not emitted for the posture.
-
-Update every exhaustive switch. Search is utility, not offense/damage; it is productive only as the
-typed pursuit. `basic_advance` (`src/vtt/snippets/registry.ts:158-202`) recognizes
-`pursue_indication` and `seek_cover` as advance options before its defense fallback; ordinary offense
-still wins. The existing Dash declaration (`offer-declarations.ts:497-506`) remains only in the normal
-branch. Keep the current action-slot/resource validations.
-
-`engineOfferableOption` hashes the canonical offer body (`src/vtt/option-modeling.ts:26-33`), so new
-objectives intentionally change IDs for the new/replaced options; unchanged normal option bodies keep
-their IDs. Never pin an ID copied from post-change output: construct the expected body by hand and
-hash it with the independent canonical-json/SHA helper already used by the tests.
-
-No-coordinate witness: deep-walk the canonical blind-posture offer body and assert (a) no opponent
-CombatantId string occurs, (b) no GridCell-shaped `{column,row}` value occurs, and (c) movement has
-only the policy tag. A control pursuit offer contains its historical cell, proving the walker is live.
-Resolved mechanics may contain the chosen cover destination; the offer body may not. Leak the sealed
-PC's `(7,2)` into the objective for the required mutant and this witness must fail.

-## 5. Productivity contract
-
-Replace the duplicated predicate with one exported structural helper owned by
-`tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:272-283`; the active v2 suite at
-`tests/unit/vtt/arena-basis-brutal-v2.test.ts:77-104` and the brutal-b membership test call it.
-A valid option is productive iff at least one holds:
-
-1. existing positive movement, attack, saving throw, cast, or world-object action;
-2. main Search paired with `pursue_indication` (movement may be 0 if already in the region); or
-3. exactly one main Dodge paired with `seek_cover`, whether movement is positive or 0.
-
-An arbitrary stationary Dodge remains unproductive. A room is unproductive precisely when at least
-one living monster has no valid option in any of those three classes. Consequently a no-indication
-monster already at best cover is productive; inability to improve cover is not failure. An unplaced,
-action-spent, or otherwise invalid actor remains unproductive if no posture resolves.
-

-| rejected/new 6209 | 36 / 46 | 36 / 36 |
-| aggregate | 185 / 251 | 185 / 185 |

-All 36 blind 6209 monsters and all 185 measured blind monsters are productive under the amended
-contract, even when a best-cover origin yields zero movement.

   193	  region, then path cost/row/column; execute existing Search after movement. It need not reach the
   194	  region this turn. Retain defensive/End Turn fallbacks.
   195	- `blind_posture`: one `Seek Cover + Dodge` composite—normal movement objective plus Dodge main
   196	  action—and End Turn. It is not Dash+Dodge; Dash consumes the same main slot and remains only in
   197	  normal declarations (`offer-declarations.ts:497-506`).
   198	
   199	`basic_advance` (`src/vtt/snippets/registry.ts:158-202`) recognizes pursuit and cover posture before
   200	its defensive fallback; ordinary offense still wins. Search is utility, not offense/damage.
   201	
   202	Offer identity is policy identity: `engineOfferableOption` hashes the canonical offer body
   203	(`src/vtt/option-modeling.ts:26-33`). Adding the typed stance/policy changes IDs of replaced/new
   204	offers; unchanged normal bodies keep IDs. A resolver-only destination/tie-order change does **not**
   205	change the policy-only offer or ID—it changes resolved mechanics/path and resolution digest. Tests
   206	hand-build canonical bodies and use the independent existing canonical-json/SHA helper.
   207	
   208	No-coordinate witness deep-walks the blind-posture offer body and asserts no opponent CombatantId and
   209	no GridCell-shaped `{column,row}` pair occurs; movement contains only the policy tag. A pursuit
   210	control contains its historical cell, proving the walker is live. Resolved mechanics may contain the
   211	chosen cover cell. Mutants that leak `(7,2)` or steer from the unseen PC without serialization fail
   212	the structural/relocation pair.

   214	## 5. Productivity contract
   215	
   216	Export one structural helper from `tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts` and make brutal-b, the v2
   217	suite after B7, and later v6 call it. A valid monster option is productive iff it has:
   218	
   219	1. existing positive movement, attack, save, cast, or world-object action; or
   220	2. Search paired with `pursue_indication` (movement may be 0 inside the region); or
   221	3. exactly one main Dodge paired with `seek_cover`, whether movement is positive or 0 and whether
   222	   all cover scores are zero/approaches empty.
   223	
   224	An ordinary stationary Dodge is not productive. A malformed/unresolvable posture is not productive.
   225	A room remains unproductive precisely when at least one living monster has no valid option in those
   226	three classes. Thus an already-best blind monster is productive, but an unplaced/action-spent actor
   227	with no valid posture can still fail.
